question: How did estimates of asteroid 2024 YR4's chance of hitting Earth change during 2025?

report.answer_text:
The estimated chance that asteroid 2024 YR4 would hit Earth on December 22, 2032 rose from about 1.2% in late January 2025 to a peak of 3.1% on February 18, then fell to nearly zero by the end of February. (assets.science.nasa.gov)
| Date in 2025 | Estimated chance of an Earth impact |
|---|---|
| Late January | About 1.2%, above the 1% threshold for issuing a formal notification. (assets.science.nasa.gov) |
| February 7 | NASA reported 2.3%. (science.nasa.gov) |
| February 18 | The estimate peaked at 3.1% for NASA and 2.8% for the European Space Agency (ESA). (science.nasa.gov) |
| February 24–25 | NASA reported 0.004% and ESA reported 0.001%. Both concluded the asteroid posed no significant threat to Earth. (science.nasa.gov) |
The asteroid’s path didn’t change; astronomers’ estimates of it did. Early observations narrowed the range of possible paths while Earth was still in that range, so a larger share of the remaining paths led to an impact. Further observations ruled out almost all of those paths. NASA’s later 2025 updates about a possible Moon impact did not raise the risk to Earth. (blogs.esa.int)
